name: SparkFun Qwiic Joystick
description: Analog 2-axis thumb joystick with push button, read over I2C: an ATtiny85 running SparkFun's firmware digitises both axes to 10 bits (0-1023, about 512 at rest) and reports the button state at I2C address 0x20 (changeable in EEPROM). Runs on 3.3 V (Qwiic); the 2.2 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups go to its supply. Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic Joystick COM-15168 (two Qwiic connectors plus a 4-pin 0.1" header: GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL), I2C address 0x20.
eli5: A little thumb stick like on a game controller; it tells your board over two wires how far you push it left/right and up/down, and whether you press it down.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (Qwiic); the on-board I2C pull-ups go to this pin

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 kOhm pull-up on board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 kOhm pull-up on board, I2C jumper)

buildNotes: Read 5 bytes starting at register 0x03: X MSB, X LSB, Y MSB, Y LSB, button. Each axis is the 10-bit ADC reading shifted left 6 bits, so value = ((MSB << 8) | LSB) >> 6.
Button register 0x07 reads 1 when released and 0 when pressed. Register 0x08 latches 1 after a press until you write 0 to it.
At rest the stick reads roughly 512 on each axis but rarely exactly; record your own centre and use a dead band (e.g. 450-575). Pushing left raises X, pushing up raises Y (SparkFun's example).
Power it from 3.3 V: the 2.2 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups go to the board's supply, so 5 V would put 5 V on an ESP32/Pico's I2C pins.
To change the address write 0x13 to register 0x09, then the new address (0x08-0x77) to 0x0A; it is kept in EEPROM. Wait about 30 ms after each write.

driver.code:
# SparkFun Qwiic Joystick (COM-15168), MicroPython driver.
# An ATtiny85 (SparkFun firmware v2.6) reads the thumb joystick's two 10 kOhm pots with its
# 10-bit ADC and serves a byte register map at I2C address 0x20:
#   0x00 ID (current I2C address)  0x01/0x02 firmware major/minor
#   0x03/0x04 X MSB/LSB  0x05/0x06 Y MSB/LSB   (10-bit reading << 6, left-justified)
#   0x07 button state (1 = released, 0 = pressed; the pin has a pull-up)
#   0x08 button status (1 = pressed since cleared; write 0 to clear)
#   0x09 I2C lock (write 0x13 first)  0x0A new I2C address (0x08-0x77, stored in EEPROM)
# The firmware streams the map from the requested register, so one 5-byte read from 0x03
# gives X, Y and the button from a single ADC update (as SparkFun's Python example does).
import time

ADDR = 0x20


class QwiicJoystick:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _read(self, reg, n):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([reg]))
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    def _write(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([reg, val]))
        time.sleep_ms(30)  # the firmware may write EEPROM; SparkFun's library waits 30 ms

    def version(self):
        d = self._read(0x01, 2)
        return d[0], d[1]

    def read(self):
        """Return (x, y, pressed): x and y are 0-1023 (about 512 at rest), pressed is True/False."""
        d = self._read(0x03, 5)
        x = ((d[0] << 8) | d[1]) >> 6
        y = ((d[2] << 8) | d[3]) >> 6
        return x, y, d[4] == 0

    def horizontal(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def vertical(self):
        return self.read()[1]

    def pressed(self):
        return self.read()[2]

    def clicked(self):
        """True if the button was pressed since the last call (reads then clears register 0x08)."""
        s = self._read(0x08, 1)[0]
        self._write(0x08, 0x00)
        return s == 1

    def set_address(self, new_addr):
        """Store a new I2C address (0x08-0x77) in the joystick's EEPROM."""
        if not 0x08 <= new_addr <= 0x77:
            raise ValueError('address must be 0x08-0x77')
        self._write(0x09, 0x13)
        self._write(0x0A, new_addr)
        self.addr = new_addr

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_joystick import QwiicJoystick

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
joy = QwiicJoystick(i2c)
while True:
    x, y, pressed = joy.read()
    print('X=%d Y=%d B=%d' % (x, y, 1 if pressed else 0))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
